panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Panel a is a patient CT arthrography image showing the captioned subchondral radiolucent fracture line, a characteristic manifestation of osteonecrosis. [raw subtype: subchondral insufficiency fracture-related osteonecrosis] b: Panel b is a patient radiograph showing collapse of the condyle lower pole and disruption of the subchondral bone plate, explicitly attributed in the caption to necrosis. [raw subtype: subchondral insufficiency fracture-related osteonecrosis] c: Panel c is a patient radiograph demonstrating the captioned subchondral separation opening under traction, consistent with the mobile subchondral fracture described as pathognomonic for necrosis. [raw subtype: subchondral insufficiency fracture-related osteonecrosis]

panels.figure_caption: Radiological pattern of a “mobile” subchondral fracture, pathognomonic for necrosis. a On CT arthrography, a very thin fracture/separation in the subchondral trabecular bone appears as a radiolucent line (“eggshell dissection”) (arrow). b A few months later, a radiograph shows a collapse of the condyle lower pole (arrow) with breaks in the continuity of the subchondral bone plate (arrowheads). c An additional radiograph performed by fluoroscopy and with traction on the leg shows a slight opening of the subchondral bone dissection (arrow)
in_text_mentions: h separation of the subchondral bone plate adherent to the cartilage from the rest of the bone (showing as a subchondral radiolucent line—the crescent sign—or “eggshell” subchondral dissection) (Fig. 8). These signs are pathognomonic of osteonecrosis, whether related to an insufficiency fracture or systemic in origin. These abnormalities can be seen on radiographic views tangent to the area of interest, possibly performed in traction to open the subchondral separation (Fig. 9a and b). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Initial radiograph demonstrates an early SIF-ON lesion with subtle hyperostosis and discrete depression near the lower pole of the femoral condyle, as specified in the caption. [raw subtype: Subchondral insufficiency fracture with osteonecrosis (SIF-ON)] b: Radiograph obtained tangent to the posteroinferior condylar pole demonstrates typical subchondral bone dissection in SIF-ON. [raw subtype: Subchondral insufficiency fracture with osteonecrosis (SIF-ON)] c: Follow-up radiograph shows progression to focal collapse of the necrotic subchondral region with complete adjacent joint-space narrowing, indicating advanced SIF-ON with secondary degenerative change. [raw subtype: Subchondral insufficiency fracture with osteonecrosis (SIF-ON)]

panels.figure_caption: Evolution of an early subchondral insufficiency fracture with osteonecrosis. a Initial radiograph shows a slight hyperostosis near a discrete depression of the lower pole of the condyle (arrow). b Additional radiograph tangent to the posteroinferior pole of the condyle and performed with traction on the leg shows a typical subchondral bone dissection (arrow). c Three months later, this necrotic area shows a focal collapse (arrows), already complicated by a complete narrowing of the adjacent joint space (arrowhead)
